albumin_creatinine.title: One urine grade, a wide range of creatinine
albumin_creatinine.alt: Six horizontal strips show measured creatinine. The grade-0 strip spans 0.6–24 mg/dL, including record 43 at 1.0.
albumin_creatinine.caption: Only identical readings are offset vertically. The grade labels show the number of patients and the scale doubles at each tick.

creatinine_hemoglobin.title: How much lower was hemoglobin at twice the creatinine?
creatinine_hemoglobin.alt: The fitted hemoglobin is 0.90 source units lower at twice the creatinine; the right-hand graphic compares predictions at 2 and 4 mg/dL.
creatinine_hemoglobin.caption: All original measured pairs are shown, including the highest creatinine value. The line joining predicted means is a model contrast across patients.

hyperglycemia.title: What did the blood test add to the diabetes history?
hyperglycemia.alt: Two strips show measured glucose. Record 43 is just above 200 mg/dL in the no-history group; 11/87 in that group and 61/125 with diabetes history reached 200.
hyperglycemia.caption: Measurements are positioned on the same linear scale. Vertical offsets separate neighboring marks. Shading denotes the study threshold, not a new diagnosis. Whole-group missing-data bounds are in the linked table.

patient_overlap.title: What else was found at urine albumin grade 0?
patient_overlap.alt: A matrix of 45 grade-zero records shows 29 with neither finding, 12 with high glucose alone, two with anemia alone and two with both. A ring marks record 43.
patient_overlap.caption: Each position corresponds to a source row, ordered by anemia, high glucose and then source row. Shapes and fills identify categories. The ring around a diamond indicates record 43.
